learningObjectives: Identify the oligodendrocyte soma, branching processes, compact myelin, internodes, paranodes and nodes of Ranvier.
Explain how myelin changes membrane capacitance and resistance to support rapid saltatory conduction.
Describe how oligodendrocytes provide metabolic support to axons in addition to electrical insulation.
Relate demyelination, remyelination and white-matter disruption to processing speed, fatigue and distributed cognitive function without over-localising symptoms.

anatomy.label: Oligodendrocyte soma
anatomy.detail: The soma contains the nucleus and biosynthetic machinery that produces the large quantities of lipid and protein required for myelin. Mature oligodendrocytes extend several processes from one compact cell body.
anatomy.clinical: Because myelin production is metabolically demanding, oligodendrocytes are vulnerable to oxidative stress, inflammation and disrupted energy supply.

anatomy.label: Myelinating processes
anatomy.detail: Branching processes contact multiple axons and form separate myelin internodes. Unlike a peripheral Schwann cell, one oligodendrocyte can myelinate portions of several central nervous system axons.
anatomy.clinical: Damage to one oligodendrocyte can therefore affect conduction across more than one axonal segment or pathway.

anatomy.label: Compact myelin
anatomy.detail: Myelin is formed when oligodendrocyte membrane wraps repeatedly around an axon and compacts into a multilamellar sheath. It raises membrane resistance and lowers capacitance across the internode.
anatomy.clinical: Myelin is not simply plastic coating. It is living membrane that must be maintained and coordinated with the axon it surrounds.

anatomy.label: Internode
anatomy.detail: An internode is the myelinated length between two nodes of Ranvier. Internode length and sheath thickness influence conduction speed and timing across a pathway.
anatomy.clinical: Distributed cognition depends on signals arriving within useful temporal windows; altered white-matter timing can disrupt coordination even when cortical regions remain structurally intact.

anatomy.label: Node of Ranvier
anatomy.detail: Nodes are short unmyelinated gaps enriched in voltage-gated sodium channels. Depolarising current travels rapidly beneath myelin, while the full action potential is regenerated at successive nodes.
anatomy.clinical: Demyelination exposes axonal membrane and redistributes current, slowing conduction or producing conduction block.

anatomy.label: Paranodal junction
anatomy.detail: Paranodal loops anchor the myelin sheath beside each node and help segregate nodal sodium channels from juxtaparanodal potassium channels. This molecular organisation preserves efficient saltatory conduction.
anatomy.clinical: Disruption of paranodal proteins can impair conduction even before gross myelin loss is obvious.

anatomy.label: Axonal metabolic support
anatomy.detail: Oligodendrocytes transfer metabolic substrates, including lactate-related energy support, to axons. This is especially important for long, active axons with limited access to extracellular nutrients beneath compact myelin.
anatomy.clinical: Axonal degeneration in white-matter disease can reflect loss of trophic and metabolic support as well as loss of insulation.

interaction.instruction: Select a myelin structure, then run the conduction sequence to compare continuous and saltatory signal propagation.
conductionSteps: An action potential reaches the first node of Ranvier and opens concentrated sodium channels.
Positive current spreads rapidly beneath the high-resistance, low-capacitance myelin internode.
The next node reaches threshold and regenerates the action potential at full amplitude.
Successive nodes repeat the process, preserving speed and reliability over distance.
The oligodendrocyte continues maintaining myelin and supplying metabolic support to the axon.

quizBank.question: Why does myelin increase conduction speed?
options: It increases membrane resistance and decreases capacitance across internodes
It releases neurotransmitter along the entire axon
It removes all sodium channels from the axon
It converts electrical signals into hormones
quizBank.explanation: Myelin limits current leak and reduces the charge needed to change membrane voltage, allowing depolarising current to spread rapidly between nodes.

quizBank.question: What is distinctive about a central nervous system oligodendrocyte?
options: One cell can myelinate segments of several axons
It myelinates only one complete peripheral axon
It functions only during childhood
It generates action potentials for nearby neurons
quizBank.explanation: A single oligodendrocyte extends multiple processes and forms separate internodes on several central nervous system axons.

quizBank.question: Where is an action potential regenerated during saltatory conduction?
options: At nodes of Ranvier
Inside compact myelin
Only at the axon hillock
Within the oligodendrocyte nucleus
quizBank.explanation: Voltage-gated sodium channels are densely concentrated at nodes of Ranvier, where the action potential is regenerated.

quizBank.question: Which statement best describes oligodendrocyte support of axons?
options: They provide both myelin and metabolic support
They provide insulation but no biological support
They remove every damaged synapse
They form the blood-brain barrier alone
quizBank.explanation: Oligodendrocytes support axons electrically through myelin and metabolically through trophic and energy-related support.

quizBank.question: Why can white-matter disruption affect cognition broadly?
options: It can disturb timing and coordination across distributed networks
White matter stores all semantic memories
It selectively suppresses one emotion centre
It affects cognition only when the frontal lobe is destroyed
quizBank.explanation: Many cognitive operations depend on precisely timed communication across distant regions, making conduction efficiency clinically important.

reviewPrompts: Explain how myelin changes membrane resistance and capacitance.
Trace saltatory conduction from one node of Ranvier to the next.
Distinguish an oligodendrocyte from a Schwann cell by the number of axonal segments myelinated.
Name one non-insulating function of oligodendrocytes.
Explain why altered white-matter timing can affect processing speed and network coordination.
